source_text: Nihil itaque in verbis tuis, coactus, ut dicis, timore praeterii. Quid enim in tam elegantis ingenii possem pavere monumentis, nisi forte hoc solum, quod horrorem de obscaenitatis tuae impugnatione perpetior?
pass_a_gloss: Nothing therefore in your words, compelled, as you say, by fear, did I pass by. For what could I have feared in the monuments of so elegant a talent, unless perhaps this alone, that I endure horror from the attacking of your obscenity?
pass_b_english: I therefore passed over nothing in your words because fear compelled me, as you say. For what could I have feared in the monuments of so refined a talent, except perhaps this alone: the horror I endure in attacking your obscenity?

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at 1.58; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
